appTagline: Urban Air Quality & Smog Day Assistant

hero.title: Plan a safer day when the air is bad
hero.body: Tell us who lives in your home and how each person travels. We fetch the air quality forecast for your city, work out when each person breathes the most smoke, and suggest changes you can actually make.
hero.step2: We check the air hour by hour
hero.step3: Get a plan with numbers you can check

plants.title: Plants for your home
plants.intro: A few easy plants that suit this household. They make a home feel fresher and calmer.
plants.honestTitle: What plants can and cannot do
plants.honest: Plants do not clean smog or PM2.5 out of a room, and a few pots will not clear the air. Closed windows in smoggy hours, an air purifier and no smoke indoors do the real work. Wipe the leaves once a week so dust does not settle on them.

light.sun: Needs a few hours of sun

plants.safeYes: Not harmful if a child or pet chews a leaf
plants.safeNo: Harmful if chewed. Keep out of reach of children and pets.

notes.child_safe: A young child lives here, so only plants that are safe if chewed are shown.
notes.asthma_mould: Someone has asthma, so plants that need constantly damp soil are left out, because damp soil can grow mould.

snake_plant.name: Snake plant
snake_plant.tip: Very hard to kill. Water it only every two weeks.

money_plant.name: Money plant (pothos)
money_plant.tip: Grows in a bottle of water or in soil. Keep it out of strong sun.

spider_plant.name: Spider plant
spider_plant.tip: Grows fast and forgives missed watering. Hang it or keep it on a shelf.

areca_palm.name: Areca palm
areca_palm.tip: Tall and leafy. Water it when the top of the soil is dry.

tulsi.name: Tulsi
tulsi.tip: Keep it where it gets morning sun, such as a balcony or a window.

rubber_plant.name: Rubber plant
rubber_plant.tip: Big shiny leaves. Wipe them with a damp cloth.

aloe_vera.name: Aloe vera
aloe_vera.tip: Likes a sunny window. Water it only when the soil is fully dry.

peace_lily.name: Peace lily
peace_lily.tip: Droops when thirsty, then stands up again after watering.

boston_fern.name: Boston fern
boston_fern.tip: Likes a damp spot, such as a bathroom with a window.

outing.title: Have to go out at a set time?
outing.intro: Tell us who is going out, when and how. We will say how the air will be at that hour and what to do.

levels.avoid: Best to wait if you can

verdict.fine: It is fine for {name} to go out at {time}
verdict.careful: {name} can go out at {time}, with care
verdict.avoid: It is better for {name} to wait if possible

outing.stricter: The advice for {name} is one step more careful than for a healthy adult, because of age or health.
outing.noCleaner: There is no clearly cleaner time within a few hours, so follow the steps below.
outing.nothingSpecial: The air is fine, so no special steps are needed.
outing.noData: There is no hourly air data to check this time.

steps.postpone: If the trip can wait, put it off to a cleaner hour.
steps.n95: Wear a well-fitted N95 or FFP2 mask. A cloth or surgical mask does not stop fine dust.
steps.mask_optional: A mask is optional. An N95 helps if the air bothers you.
steps.infant_indoors: Do not put a mask on a baby. Keep the time outside as short as you can, or keep the baby indoors.
steps.inhaler: Carry the inhaler or reliever medicine where you can reach it.
steps.heart_slow: Walk slowly and stop to rest. Do not hurry or climb stairs fast.
steps.elderly_company: Go with someone, and keep a phone and any medicines with you.
steps.pregnant_short: Keep the time outside as short as possible, and rest indoors when you return.
steps.walk_slow: Walk slowly and breathe through the nose. Use lanes away from heavy traffic.
steps.helmet_mask: On an open vehicle you breathe the road air. If you wear a mask, put it on under the helmet or scarf.
steps.recirculate: Keep the windows shut and set the AC to recirculate.
steps.quiet_road: This is rush hour. Take a quieter road if there is one.
steps.break_indoors: On a long trip, take a break indoors in between.
steps.after_wash: When you return, wash your face and hands, and change clothes if you can.
steps.symptoms: If you cough, wheeze, feel dizzy or have chest pain, stop, go indoors and rest. See a doctor if it does not settle. For chest pain or trouble breathing, get help straight away.

advisory.intro: Write a short notice you can post in a residents' group or send to a school.
advisory.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

footer.disclaimer: AuraGuide AI gives general guidance and is not medical advice. If you have a heart or lung condition, follow your doctor's advice.
footer.dataCredit: Air quality data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0). AQI follows the CPCB National AQI bands used in India.
footer.method: How the numbers work: each person's exposure adds up the PM2.5 they breathe hour by hour, weighted for age and health. Emissions use a fixed factor per kilometre for each kind of transport.
